title: Retry-safe SDDC Manager network-pool reconciliation
prompt:
Complete the root Go package `networkpoolensure` (module `vcf91-0036`, standard library only) as a focused VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 SDDC Manager REST integration. Creating a network pool is a POST, but callers must be able to retry an ensure operation after an uncertain transport outcome without creating the same pool twice. Collection output must also remain deterministic when SDDC Manager changes element order.

Before implementing, research the `getNetworkPool`, `createNetworkPool`, and `getNetworksOfNetworkPool` operations in the SDDC Manager OpenAPI specification in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository and cite the specification URLs consulted. Do not contact any other SDDC Manager route.

Preserve the public models and error types declared in `client.go` and implement these rules:

- `NewClient(Config)` treats `BaseURL` as an HTTP(S) origin and performs no traffic. Reject embedded credentials, query (including a dangling `?`), fragment, a non-root path, and a blank or ASCII-whitespace-bearing access token. A nil HTTP client means `http.DefaultClient`. Copy the selected HTTP client and disable redirect following without mutating the caller's client.
- `ListNetworkPools(ctx)` invokes exactly `GET /v1/network-pools`, with no query or body. Send `Accept: application/json` and `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; do not send `Content-Type` or a dangling query delimiter. Accept exactly HTTP 200 with an `application/json` media type. Require `elements` and `pageMetadata`, validate the live `totalElements` value against the actual element count without requiring absent pagination members, and require nonblank unique pool IDs and nonblank names. Preserve every decoded field, including the shallow network-ID projections returned by this collection. Return a copy sorted by `name`, then `id`, using Go's case-sensitive string ordering. Return a non-nil empty slice for an empty collection and never return service order.
- `EnsureNetworkPool(ctx, spec)` validates before traffic. `Name` must be nonblank with no surrounding whitespace and `Networks` must contain at least one network. Each network requires a nonblank, trimmed `Type`; `VLANID` and `MTU` must fit signed int32. Presence-aware optional strings reject empty, surrounding-whitespace values; `IPAddressVersion`, when present, is `IPv4` or `IPv6`, and `IPAddressAssignmentMode` is `STATIC`, `DHCP`, or `SLAAC`. Every IP pool requires trimmed, nonblank `Start` and `End` values.
- Serialize `NetworkPoolSpec` once as compact UTF-8 JSON. Required request members are `name`, `networks`, and, within each network, `type`, `vlanId`, and `mtu`. Unset optional fields must be absent rather than null or empty. Never send read-only `id`, `hostsCount`, `freeIps`, `usedIps`, `usedIpCount`, or `freeIpCount` in the create body.
- Reconcile under a per-client, context-interruptible gate so concurrent ensures for the same client cannot race into duplicate POSTs. First call `getNetworkPool`. If no pool has the requested name, invoke exactly `POST /v1/network-pools` once, with no query, the same GET headers plus `Content-Type: application/json`, and the serialized body. Accept exactly HTTP 201 `application/json` and require a nonblank returned ID plus the requested name; do not require the POST response to echo writable network configuration. Then invoke `getNetworksOfNetworkPool` as exactly `GET /v1/network-pools/{id}/networks`, require `elements` and live `pageMetadata.totalElements`, attach those detailed networks to the returned pool, and require the writable configuration to equal the request. Return `Created: true`.
- If exactly one listed pool has the requested name, retrieve its detailed networks with `getNetworksOfNetworkPool`; if that writable configuration equals the request, return the hydrated pool with `Created: false` and send no POST. If its writable configuration differs, return `*DriftError`; if multiple listed pools have the name, return `*AmbiguousMatchError`. Neither case may mutate. This lookup-before-create rule is the retry guarantee: do not automatically retry POST. If a POST commits but its response is lost, that call returns a transport error; a later call must discover the committed pool through GET and must not POST again.
- Bound response bodies to 1 MiB, close every body, reject malformed, trailing, oversized, or wrong-media-type success data with `*ProtocolError`, and stop traffic after a failure. Decode non-success error envelopes into `*APIError`, preserving operationId, status, errorCode, message, remediationMessage, and referenceToken. Use `*TransportError` for transport/read failures and preserve causes for `errors.Is`/`errors.As`, including context cancellation. Error strings must not expose the bearer token, response body, decoded server/remediation message, reference token, or underlying transport exception text.

Do not modify `go.mod`, `contract_test.go`, `.gitignore`, or `internal/contractmock/`; edit only `client.go`. Run `go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30s ./...`.
